messages:
Alex CSM: Putting together a short customer-facing runbook for launch windows — focus: prefill/warm-pool, client batching guidance, and streaming fallbacks. Sharing draft for quick feedback.
Jamie Eng: Nice. Keep it short. Can we standardize metrics to include p50/p90 latency and prefill_cost per-hour?
Alex CSM: Yes. Proposed metrics: prefill_cost, prefills_active, prefill_latency_p50, prefill_latency_p90, stream_error_rate.
Noah PM: Also include a ‘budget cap’ option customers can set so we can signal before spend breaches.
Lin SRE: For behavior: recommend enabling warm-pool only for ramp windows and critical renewals. Implementation notes: warm-pool uses sticky routing + tenant affinity; add circuit-breaker that drops to on-demand model if cost delta > X in 30m.
Alex CSM: Draft guidance block for customers:
```
What we do:
 - Prefill: we make requests to keep a small pool of ready workers for your tenant during the launch window so initial requests are low-latency.
 - Batching: we recommend a short client-side batching window (50-200ms) when possible to reduce cost.
 - Streaming fallback: if streaming interrupts, the client should retry with a single non-stream request and show a progress indicator.
Why it helps:
 - Lower cold-start latency
 - Reduced token cost via batching and cache reuse
 - Safer ramping with automated scale-down
```
Emily CS: I'll turn that into a two-paragraph kickoff blurb and an optional FAQ item about cost controls.
Maya CS: Adding feedback capture: 72h automated check-in + one-click NPS-ish question and latency thumbs up/down. Short form: 3 quick Qs + open comment.
Devon Eng: Implementation notes for Eng team:
 - Gate under feature flag: `cs.ramp_v2`
 - Emit metrics: `console.prefill_cost` (USD/hr), `console.prefills_active`, `console.prefill_latency_p50`, `console.prefill_latency_p90`, `console.stream_error_rate`
 - Alert: Alert when prefill_cost > budget_cap * 1.2 within 1h OR stream_error_rate > 5% for 15m.
Jamie Eng: Add sample curl and minimal SDK snippet for partners to trigger a manual prefill (useful for partner-led staging):
```
# curl example
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prefill \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"T-ACME","prefill_seconds":900,"max_workers":4,"reason":"launch-window"}'

# python SDK minimal
client.prefill(tenant_id='T-ACME', seconds=900, max_workers=4)
```
Lin SRE: Ops checklist for handoff:
 - Confirm budget_cap on account and set alert thresholds
 - Enable warm-pool for window and tag nodes with `cs.ramp`
 - Ensure sticky routing for tenant during window
 - Have fallback route (cheaper model) configured if circuit-breaker trips
Onboard-bot: Reminder scheduled: add post-launch 72h survey + attach CS note to account record.
Alex CSM: Decision items: set default prefill_ttl=1800s, high_risk_ttl=300s, backoff_ttl=7200s. Define high-risk triggers: >2 failed renewal touches OR usage drop >25% week-over-week.
Maya CS: I'll add the survey link and prefill the questions. Emily will draft the kickoff email.
Jamie Eng: Dashboard panels I'll add: Prefill cost over time, active prefills by tenant, p90 latency, stream error rate, and a list of tenants with budget breach alerts.
Noah PM: Can we add a short customer-facing toggle copy for console: "Enable Launch Prefill (we'll keep a warm pool during your selected window; you control budget caps)"
Alex CSM: Yes — Emily/Maya to author copy. Devon/Lin to add feature flag and alerts. I'll run a 15m sync tomorrow 10:30 PT to finalize. Thanks everyone :pray:
root_message: Alex CSM: Putting together a short customer-facing runbook for launch windows — focus: prefill/warm-pool, client batching guidance, and streaming fallbacks. Sharing draft for quick feedback.
